name: Halcyon Variform Lace Boot
description:
A clean, utilitarian ankle boot with a modular toe box that expands or contracts via a small dial recessed into the heel. Designed for augmented feet with variable geometry — servos, hydraulic toes, or swappable foot attachments — the Variform can accommodate foot widths from narrow standard to nearly twice that. The upper is a durable waxed canvas in olive or charcoal, with minimal branding.

The Tier 3 crowd appreciates that it doesn't scream 'prosthetic accommodation' — it just looks like a well-made boot. Worn by office workers, mid-level techs, and anyone who doesn't want their augmentation to define their wardrobe.
functionality: Dial-adjust toe box expands/contracts to fit variable-geometry augmented feet. Accommodates most standard prosthetic foot attachments.
what_it_says: Understated, practical, and quietly well-considered. You've done your research.
worn_by: Tier 3 daily commuters with prosthetic feet
story_hooks: The dial mechanism is precise enough to detect micro-changes in a prosthetic's geometry — a worn pair could tell you someone has recently swapped or damaged their foot attachment.
A specific batch of Variform boots was recalled after the dial mechanism was found to interfere with certain military-grade prosthetic calibration systems.
